A sudden rise often means something is stuck, such as a sync loop or a buggy update, rather than how you use it.
New background drainers are often a recent install or update that keeps working when you aren\'t using it.
Background work keeps the processor and radios busy, which drains the battery while you aren\'t looking.
While a wakelock is held the phone can\'t sleep, so the battery drains even with the screen off.
Each wakeup pulls the phone out of sleep. Many of them add up and keep Doze from engaging.
Jobs and syncs can wake the phone and use the network. Frequent activity can keep it from resting.
Deep Doze is how Android saves battery overnight. Without it, standby drain is higher.
Exempt apps keep running when Android would otherwise pause them, so their background work costs more.
Screen-off drain is battery you lose without using the phone. Higher than usual usually means something keeps it awake.
A lasting change shows up here before it is obvious day to day.
Sitting at full charge for long periods ages a battery faster, especially when it\'s warm.
Heat is the main thing that wears a battery out. Charging while hot speeds that up.
Less capacity means shorter battery life per charge. Every battery wears with age, but charging habits can slow it down.
Location and sensor activity can use battery in the background. The measured counter shows which activity was observed.
An active mobile radio uses a lot of power and stays on for a while after each transfer.
A foreground service keeps the app alive and allowed to work, even when you think it is closed.
It shows whether the fix seems to help, so you can keep it or undo it.
Not proof the app is broken. Android reports per-app time and activity, not exact battery energy, and heavy use you chose counts too.
Not a measure of energy. Background time, wakeups and jobs are signs of activity, and the app may need some of them for messages, music or navigation.
Not tied to one app. Named wakelocks and wakeup reasons are session hints, not proof of the cause.
Not a cause. A change in how you use the phone shows up here too.
Not damage already done. Heat and long hours at full add wear over months; one session matters little.
Not an exact capacity. Estimates vary from charge to charge; the trend over weeks matters more than one value.
An association, not proof. Other changes in the same days affect the numbers too.
